text.p: Italian bonds and futures started on a firmer track largely in a rebound after Monday's losses helped by the steady trend in bunds and the lira, dealers said.

They added that doubts remained about the EMU stability pact with EU commissioner for monetary affairs Yves Thibault de Silguy saying the EU needs to stick by the agreed EMU schedule. This came after France's new Socialist-led government called on Monday for a "period of reflection" on the stability pact.
"The market is ticking up after yesterday's losses but the mood is cautious and futures will be volatile to any developments on EMU," one LIFFE dealer said.

Dealers said that the French position over EMU was leading to uncertainties, and the BTP market would continue to show a volatile trend, with selling pressure from yesterday being followed by a period of reflection in early trading today.
They pointed out that until there was some clarity over the French position on EMU, market volatility was likely to continue especially for high yielding bonds like BTPs.
"Today's rally could push a little higher but sellers will emerge around 130 on the September contract," said the dealer. The Sept BTP futures LIFFE contract hit an early high of 129.79.
